decisions_for_user: CI's three failures are ONE cause and it is the test harness, not the product (F285). The suite runs in-memory, whose SQLAlchemy pool is a StaticPool -- every AsyncSession shares one connection, so any request finishing rolls back whatever a background run is writing. Reproduced on this machine with CI's exact error (scripts/drive/churn_sessions_plugin.py, CHURN_DELAY=0.3) and shown not to occur on a file-backed engine, which is the only kind production uses. WHICH FIX is the operator's call: an unshared pool, a file-backed temp database per test, or per-test engine disposal. They differ in how much of the suite has to be re-timed. Until one is chosen the branch cannot satisfy the merge gate's condition 3.

F286 (B) is the part of the CI red that is NOT a harness problem and outlives its fix: _execute_run's exception handler gates the queue redrain on `already_terminal`, so an exception raised after a run reaches a terminal status leaves the input queued behind it undrained, with nothing on a timer to notice. It is a candidate for D-4's spec slot if the drive produces nothing stronger.

The merge gate remains dormant because STATE-day.json's seeded limits[0] still forbids merges. Conditions 1, 2 and 4 passed this morning; only CI (condition 3) failed, and D-2 has now explained why. Whether to hand the fast-forward step over to the day window is the operator's call.
